title: 271 days of AI-assisted development and I got my first game out - Wizards of Elnia
author: Vivid_Pickle_8336
selftext:
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5222880/Wizards\_of\_Elnia/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5222880/Wizards_of_Elnia/)  
  
Hi!  
Wasn't sure I wanted to make this thread but here goes: I finally finished my first game.  
It started in February with a simple Claude prompt to test how good it was. It was a game with literally 2 boxes shooting spheres, lightning and boomerangs.   
5271 prompts and hours on hours of testing later this is my result.

I will have to say it straight - I do not like AI art and AI assets. Unfortunately, I was not gifted enough to do it by hands, I tried many times, trust me. So I went with it for now. I have already done a significant part of work to remove a lot of it but it's still a long way to go.

With that out the way - a bit about my game. As it's usually suggested for the new game devs - I went with a simple idea. Obvious mechanics, lots of variety, steady progression.

If you ever played custom maps in Warcraft 3 - you will recognize this immediately. It is basically warlocks but reworked and (hopefully) improved upon. The idea is that it's a shrinking arena with up to 8 players/bots. You have 5 combat slots, 1 mobility and 1 defensive + a melee skill that's the same for everyone. You fill that up from a selection of 52 spells. Wild combos, different playstyles and close calls is what I went for. To make it not-so-overwhelming I implemented a progression system. Simple account levels with XP earned for every match. This allowed to not dump everything on the player but let him gradually walk deeper. First few games are testing the flow, then new spells unlock, then some account features and then advanced combinations. This is probably something that I'm sure of the most - it's easy to start and it keeps you wondering what awaits next.  
You can check it on steam for a more detailed explanation.

**Now for the technical parts**

I need to start with me being an experienced developer. Around 15 years of experience of coding in very different languages and technologies. My career is Android but lately iOS as well.  
With this project I went with AI at maximum. First I started with Claude but then switched to Codex mid way. Game's written in Godot (a decision I've come to regret later) and it's currently available for win, mac, linux. I'm not even sure how many custom skills for this I wrote but the main beneficiary of that is the build system. Windows + mac are built on my mac and linux is built on my gaming PC in parallel. Everything is packaged together and is uploaded to steam. If I'm being honest - I would probably not be able to consistently reproduce this build process on my own.  
Here's why. I have decided to build my launcher client. Think League of Legends. I came to an understanding that Godot's UI framework is horrible and no amount of research, fixes, prompting or manual editing helped make it look good and usable. When I was making a game without AI I always thought it was a skill issue. Nope, it's just bad. So instead I asked Codex to help me build a launcher client on a nice tech stack, he suggested Slint and I went with it. Wasn't an easy process but eventually it worked out. It still has its rough edges but I'm fixing them one by one. I have never heard about Slint before this and I would never take a Rust/C++ technology to try something like this. 

What I enjoyed the most about the process of creating this game is that my game design skills became the main focus. I could think of the spells, create combinations, balance things out and just systematically save this info on paper. After that just feeding it to codex helped me avoid so much routine work that it could probably be measured in hundreds and hundreds of hours. 

For me this project is a dream come true. I have never imagined that I would be able to make my own game with a concept I've been honing for years let alone release it on steam. I'm currently in the process of finishing the ports to mobile platforms and with that I will be able to cover everything non-console. Oh, if you have a steam deck or any other handheld device - you can also fully play with it. A special gamepad layout is there and it made me sweat a bit but it's very much playable. 

Thanks to everyone who read till the end! I really hope some of you try it out and especially get a few friends to check it out as well. It's incredibly fun with at least 4-5 players and pretty much every single person that tested it said the same.
